abstract: Temporal audio grounding requires locating every occurrence of a queried target, making both occurrence counts and interval boundaries essential. We propose RefTAG, a post-training framework for verifiable temporal self-correction. Its Reflection Chain-of-Thought (Re-CoT) protocol combines draft intervals, discrete count and boundary actions, and revised intervals in one response. Supervised fine-tuning on these trajectories (Re-CoT-SFT) teaches the protocol; reinforcement learning (RL) jointly rewards final localization and revision outcomes. Across 8,228 queries, Re-CoT-SFT improves query-weighted mIoU over final-answer SFT by 1.74 percentage points. RL further improves TAG-Bench multi-target mIoU by 0.40 points and R@0.5 by 0.86 points. The final model achieves 38.50% TAG-Bench mIoU and 51.01% mean mIoU across three datasets, outperforming the evaluated open-source MOSS-Audio and FireRedAudio models and the commercial Gemini-3.1-Pro on both measures. These results demonstrate that explicitly coupling count- and boundary-aware revision with joint reward optimization provides an effective and verifiable path to temporal audio grounding.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对自然语言查询在音频中所有出现位置都要找全找准的问题，RefTAG 让模型先写草稿区间再做数量与边界诊断并给出修订，并用最终定位质量与修订效果的联合奖励做强化学习，在 8228 条查询上把平均定位精度做到 51.01%，代价是一次回答要走完草稿加诊断加修订的完整结构。
originalTitle: RefTAG: Reflection-aware Temporal Audio Grounding in Large Audio Language Models
readerTitle: 先给草稿再自我修正：RefTAG 如何做语音中的时间定位
